title: What skills, fit and proper and governance requirements apply to superannuation trustee boards?
description: What APRA's SPS 510 and SPS 520 require of RSE licensee directors and responsible persons, how FAR overlaps, and what the 2028 CPS 510 reforms change.
shortAnswer: The Australian Prudential Regulation Authority (APRA) requires registrable superannuation entity (RSE) licensees to keep a board whose directors and senior managers collectively have the full range of skills needed, to assess board and director performance at least annually under Prudential Standard SPS 510 Governance, and to assess every responsible person as fit and proper before appointment and annually under SPS 520 Fit and Proper. A consolidated CPS 510 is proposed to replace both from January 1, 2028.
keyTakeaways: SPS 510 and SPS 520, both in force since June 30, 2024, require collective board skills, a board renewal policy, annual board and individual director performance assessments, and documented competencies for every responsible person position.

A fit and proper assessment must be completed before a person takes a responsible person position, repeated annually (or as close to annually as practicable), and documented well enough to show fitness and propriety.
Since March 15, 2025 the Financial Accountability Regime has also applied to superannuation trustees, so directors and senior executives sit under two overlapping regimes.

APRA's draft CPS 510, released for consultation on June 16, 2026, would require a board skills matrix with measurable proficiency scales, cap non-executive director tenure at 12 years, narrow responsible persons to align with FAR, and commence on January 1, 2028.
None of these standards prescribes training hours. Capability is evidenced through skills assessment, performance reviews and documented action on gaps.
appliesTo: RSE licensees (superannuation trustees) under the Superannuation Industry (Supervision) Act 1993
Directors, or individual trustees in a group of individual trustees
Senior managers, the RSE licensee secretary, RSE auditors and RSE actuaries
People in connected entities whose activities could materially affect the RSE licensee's business operations or financial standing

sections.heading: Which APRA standards set governance and fit and proper requirements for super trustees?

blocks.text: Two superannuation prudential standards made under section 34C of the Superannuation Industry (Supervision) Act 1993 (SIS Act) set the requirements: [SPS 510 Governance](https://www.apra.gov.au/standards/sps-510) and [SPS 520 Fit and Proper](https://www.apra.gov.au/standards/sps-520). The current versions of both were determined on June 3, 2024 and commenced on June 30, 2024, and they apply to all RSE licensees.

SPS 510 sets out the board's responsibilities, the governance framework, board composition, performance assessment, renewal, nomination and the Board Audit Committee. SPS 520 sets the fit and proper criteria, the content of the Fit and Proper Policy, assessment timing and notification to APRA. SPS 521 Conflicts of Interest sits alongside them. These requirements are prudential, not conduct based, and they are separate from the operational risk duties described on the [APRA CPS 230](/regulations/apra-cps-230-operational-risk-training) page.

blocks.title: Currency and transition
blocks.text: This page reflects SPS 510 and SPS 520 as at November 2026. APRA consulted until August 28, 2026 on a draft cross industry CPS 510 that would consolidate SPS 510, SPS 520, SPS 521 and CPS 520. APRA plans to release the final standard in late 2026; the draft commences on January 1, 2028. Until then, SPS 510 and SPS 520 remain the operative standards.

sections.heading: What does SPS 510 require of board skills and performance?

blocks.text: SPS 510 requires the board to ensure that directors and senior management collectively have the full range of skills needed for the effective and prudent operation of the RSE licensee, and that each director has skills allowing an effective contribution to board deliberations. The standard specifies that directors collectively must have "the necessary skills, knowledge and experience to understand the risks of the RSE licensee's business operations, including its legal and prudential obligations".

items: **Performance assessment:** the board must have procedures for assessing, at least annually, the board's performance against its objectives, and the performance of individual directors.
**Renewal:** the board must have a formal renewal policy describing how it will remain open to new ideas and independent thinking while retaining adequate expertise.

**Nomination and tenure:** policies must address term length, maximum tenure, how candidate suitability is assessed, and the factors for reappointment, including whether length of service could interfere with acting in beneficiaries' best interests.
**External expertise:** the board may supplement its skills by engaging external consultants and experts, which does not remove the collective skills obligation.
**Residency:** senior management must be ordinarily resident in Australia, and a majority of directors must be ordinarily resident in Australia.

blocks.text: Because the obligation is collective, the practical tool is a board [skills matrix](/glossary/skills-matrix) that maps required capabilities to current directors and identifies gaps for recruitment or development. SPS 510 does not itself require a matrix, but the draft replacement standard does.

sections.heading: What does SPS 520 require for fit and proper assessments?

blocks.text: SPS 520 requires an RSE licensee to define and document the competencies required for each responsible person position and to assess every responsible person against fit and proper criteria before appointment and annually after that. Responsible persons include directors, the secretary, senior managers, the RSE auditor or lead auditor, the RSE actuary, and people in connected entities whose activities could materially affect the RSE licensee. A person need not be an employee to be a responsible person.

The criteria in paragraph 19 are whether it would be prudent to conclude that the person possesses "the competence, character, diligence, experience, honesty, integrity and judgement" to perform the duties properly; whether they possess the education or technical qualifications, knowledge and skills relevant to the duties of an RSE licensee; whether they are disqualified under the SIS Act; and whether any conflict would create a material risk of failing to perform properly. RSE auditors need a minimum of five years' relevant audit experience with RSE licensees, and RSE actuaries five years' relevant experience and Fellow or Accredited Member status with the Institute of Actuaries of Australia.

blocks.text: The Fit and Proper Policy must be approved by the board, form part of the risk management framework, state who conducts assessments, what information is obtained, and the decision process, and be given to each director candidate as soon as possible after nomination. Its whistleblowing provisions must be adequately explained to directors and employees likely to hold relevant information, which is one of the few places SPS 520 directly implies a communication or training activity.

sections.heading: How does the Financial Accountability Regime overlap with these standards?

blocks.text: The Financial Accountability Regime (FAR) applied to superannuation trustees from March 15, 2025, so most RSE licensee directors and senior executives are now both responsible persons under SPS 520 and accountable persons under FAR. APRA's [FAR page](https://www.apra.gov.au/cross-industry/financial-accountability-regime-far) confirms that FAR is jointly administered by APRA and the Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC), and commenced for banks on March 15, 2024 and for insurers and superannuation trustees on March 15, 2025.

The regimes ask different questions. SPS 520 asks whether a person is suitable to hold the role, at appointment and each year. FAR asks whether an accountable person met their accountability obligations, including taking reasonable steps within their area of responsibility. Capability evidence serves both: a documented assessment of a director's skills against the role supports the fit and proper conclusion, and a record of targeted development supports a reasonable steps argument. The [Financial Accountability Regime training](/regulations/financial-accountability-regime-training) page covers FAR obligations in detail.

APRA's [governance review consultation paper](https://www.apra.gov.au/governance-review-consultation-paper) states that FAR "remains the primary mechanism for accountability of senior executives and directors", while fit and proper requirements focus on suitability at appointment and ongoing oversight. It proposes narrowing responsible persons to accountable persons, auditors, actuaries and RSE licensee secretaries, and removing routine fit and proper reporting, which APRA says would mean forms are no longer required for 6,000 individuals.

sections.heading: What will the proposed CPS 510 change for super boards?

blocks.text: The draft CPS 510 would raise the bar on documenting and measuring board capability. APRA's [consultation page](https://www.apra.gov.au/consultations/proposed-changes-governance) says the paper was released on June 16, 2026, consultation closed on August 28, 2026, the final standard and guidance are planned for late 2026, and the new requirements are expected to take effect from early 2028. The draft standard itself states a commencement date of January 1, 2028.

items: **Skills matrix:** paragraph 47 of the draft requires a documented board skills matrix covering skills, experience and behavioral attributes, having regard to strategy, risk appetite and likely future needs; paragraph 48 requires "clear assessment criteria and rating scales of proficiency that can be measured and verified".
**Addressing gaps:** under paragraph 49 the board must be able to demonstrate how it is actively addressing current or future skill and capability deficiencies.

**Performance assessment:** annual assessment of the board, committees and individual directors against objectives and the skills matrix, with significant financial institutions also needing an external independent assessment at least every three years.

**Tenure:** non-executive directors limited to 12 years in total, with a board approved extension of up to 12 months in exceptional circumstances notified to APRA within 10 days. APRA notes this reflects an expectation already in its guidance for superannuation.

**Fit and proper criteria:** assessments would have to consider professional references, findings of courts, tribunals, regulators and inquiries, and, for directors, the skills needed under the board skills matrix.

blocks.text: For training teams, measurable proficiency scales are the significant change. A self rating of "strong" against a skill label will be hard to defend; a [proficiency scale](/glossary/proficiency-scale) with defined levels and evidence for each rating is what the draft describes.

sections.heading: What capability evidence should an RSE licensee keep?

blocks.text: An RSE licensee should be able to show, for each responsible person, the competencies the role requires, how the person was assessed against them, and what was done about any gap. sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry structures a trustee's governance obligations, position competency profiles and skills matrix as one framework, so each proficiency rating links to the knowledge it requires and the evidence that supports it. When APRA finalizes CPS 510, the changed criteria can be traced to the affected positions and assessments rather than rebuilt from scratch.

faqs.q: Do super fund directors have mandatory training hours?
faqs.a: No. SPS 510 and SPS 520 do not set training hours or a qualification for directors. They require collective board skills, documented competencies for each responsible person position, and annual assessment. Training is one way to close a gap that an assessment identifies, and the board must be able to show how gaps are being addressed.

APRA has proposed consolidating SPS 510, SPS 520, SPS 521 and CPS 520 into a single cross industry CPS 510. Consultation closed on August 28, 2026, the final standard is planned for late 2026, and the draft commences on January 1, 2028. SPS 520 continues to apply until then.

faqs.q: Can an RSE licensee appoint someone before a fit and proper assessment is finished?
faqs.a: Only as an interim appointment for up to 90 days, or longer with APRA's written agreement, and only after reasonable steps specified in the Fit and Proper Policy have been taken to assess the person. A full assessment must be completed before the appointment becomes permanent.

faqs.q: Does FAR replace fit and proper for super trustees?
faqs.a: No. Both apply. FAR governs accountability of accountable persons, while SPS 520 governs suitability for responsible person positions. APRA proposes to reduce duplication by aligning the responsible person cohort with FAR and relying on FAR reporting instead of routine fit and proper forms, but the proposal is not yet final.

SPS 520: assessment before appointment, 28 days for APRA determined responsible persons, interim appointment up to 90 days, annual reassessment, documentation retention, whistleblowing provisions explained to directors and employees, SRS 520.0 notification within 14 days
